excluded_from_core_matrix.reason: The unified-diff v1 pilot tested the same task and deployments as the later whole-file run. It remains transport evidence but is not counted as a fourth independent task.
Smoke runs preceded their frozen comparison plans.

source_reports.role: core frozen comparison with layered transport evidence

best_known_requirement_evidence.evidence_basis: retrospective v1.2 replay of exact saved v1.1 artifacts
one preregistered and three explicitly post-hoc code-byte-identical transport checks

qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mxfp8.observed_boundary: Produced usable artifacts in all three core comparisons but did not satisfy any complete current verifier.

qwen3.8:27b-mlx.observed_boundary: Closest JavaScript candidate and verifier-confirmed PHP code, but the frozen Python pass became a false positive under the corrected verifier.

gpt-oss:20b.observed_boundary: Consumed the 3,000-token budget in hidden reasoning and emitted no visible artifact in all three core comparisons; this is a deployment-setting and harness-fit result, not proof of absent coding knowledge.

muse-glimmer:30b-mlx.observed_boundary: Solved the corrected Python requirements and produced verifier-confirmed PHP code, but failed JavaScript invalidation races and used comparatively long outputs and wall time.

ornith-1.5:35b.observed_boundary: Solved the corrected Python requirements and produced verifier-confirmed PHP code with the shortest successful cold wall times, but failed the JavaScript concurrency task.

interpretation.central_finding: No deployment dominated across the three tasks. Observed coding capability changed with task semantics, language, artifact transport and verifier strength.
interpretation.harness_finding: The PHP comparison shows that strict artifact delivery and code semantics are distinct outcomes. Track B should test whether file-writing tools remove this transport floor.
interpretation.verifier_finding: The pagination false positive shows that a stronger model score is meaningless when the verifier omits an explicit requirement.
interpretation.routing_finding: The sample is too small for a router, but already rejects a universal model ranking and motivates task-conditional least-cost sufficient configurations.
interpretation.next_experiment: Run the same frozen fixtures and strongest available verifiers under two separately reported Track B harnesses: pinned Pi and the project mini-harness.

limitations: One attempt per task and deployment cannot estimate stochastic reliability or latency distributions.
The tasks differ in language and task family, so language effects cannot be separated from task effects.
The best-known evidence matrix mixes frozen, preregistered-secondary and explicitly post-hoc evidence and is not a formal leaderboard.
Parameter count, quantization, runtime implementation and memory use differ between deployments.
No tested deployment solved the JavaScript case, so no least-cost sufficient configuration exists for that task in this sample.
